subject: Geo-binding commitments & KMS control for Private deployment

From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@ferryhealth.com>

Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Geo-binding commitments & KMS control for Private deployment

Hi Sean,

Thanks for taking this. We are finalizing requirements for a Private (VPC) deployment and need crisp answers for our security and procurement teams. Short bullets below — can you confirm which of these Redwood can commit to in writing, and what the operational constraints are?

1) Region binding: can you guarantee the tenant's persistent storage (model artifacts, logs, and customer prompt data) will never be written outside the contracted region except under an explicit DR invocation?

2) Customer-held keys: does Redwood support customer-managed KMS (BYOK) for disk and object encryption for Private deployments? If so, what are the flows for key rotation and emergency key revocation?

3) Deletion and attestations: upon contract termination or tenant decommission, can you provide an auditable wipe and a signed attestation? What's the expected timeline and what logs are produced?

4) Cross-region failover: if the customer enables cross-region failover, can you guarantee no background replication occurs to the DR region until failover is triggered?

5) Evidence and certification: what artifacts (audit logs, wipe job manifests, snapshots of storage allocation records) can you provide to satisfy our compliance team?

I've attached a short PDF with Ferry's security checklist. We need answers by close of business Thursday to keep the procurement cadence.

Thanks,
Maria Gonzalez
Director, Security Operations
Ferry Health

Subject: Re: Geo-binding commitments & KMS control for Private deployment

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear checklist. High level answers below; I'll follow with a short playbook and suggested contractual language.

1) Region binding
- For Private/VPC deployments we run tenant data on disks logically scoped to the customer's designated cloud region/az. For managed Private (Redwood-operated VPC), we can commit to a contractual region-binding SOW: storage will be provisioned in the agreed region and will not be replicated to other regions except under a documented DR activation.
- Note: platform control-plane metadata (control plane APIs, billing records) may reside in Redwood control plane regions for management and do not contain customer PII or model prompt payloads. We can enumerate those fields in the SOW.

2) Customer-held keys (BYOK)
- Yes, we support customer-managed KMS (BYOK) for disk and object encryption for Private deployments. Options:
  a) Customer KMS in their cloud account (recommended): Redwood runs in the customer's VPC and leverages the customer's KMS for volume and object keys. Redwood never holds plaintext keys.
  b) Dedicated HSM/KMS integration (enterprise): we can integrate with customer HSMs via standard KMS APIs.
- Key rotation: rotation is performed by the customer's KMS. Redwood supports rolling re-encryption hooks; we coordinate key rotation windows to avoid latent cache issues (typical window: <1 hour).
- Emergency revocation: if the customer revokes keys, volumes become unreadable; we recommend a formal joint runbook to avoid accidental data loss. We can document a 3-step emergency key-revoke/RTO procedure in the SOW.

3) Deletion and attestations
- Deletion: for Private deployments we execute a multi-phase deletion: stop services, zero-fill (where supported by the cloud provider), run secure delete jobs on object stores (object lifecycle + overwrite where applicable), and then release volumes.
- Timeline: typical complete device-level wipe for a tenant is 5–7 business days depending on data size and provider APIs; we will provide a certificate of deletion within 10 business days post-start.
- Artifacts: we can provide (a) job run logs (start/end/exit code), (b) storage provider object lifecycle records, (c) checksums/hashes of deleted manifests, and (d) the signed deletion attestation.

4) Cross-region failover
- We do not enable asynchronous replication to a DR region by default. Cross-region replication is an opt-in configuration with flags that explicitly enable replication. If Ferry opts into a DR footprint we will document the replication policy and include explicit customer approval gates.

5) Evidence and certification
- We can produce: audit logs (tenant-level access, API calls with timestamps), wipe job manifests, KMS audit events (subject to customer's KMS exportability), and a signed attestation. For SOC2/ISO asks, we can provide mapped artifacts and a letter of attestation.

Next steps: I'm attaching a short playbook (redwood-geobind-playbook-v1.pdf) and a draft SOW addendum with proposed binding language around region and deletion. If this looks good I'll convert the SOW to a DocuSign envelope for signature and add the deletion SLA to the contract.

We can meet Wednesday to walk legal/procurement through the exact wording. Does 09/15 11:00 PT work for you?

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Technical Sales (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference

Thanks Sean — clear and helpful. A couple of quick clarifications before legal signs off:

> 1) Region binding — you say the control plane metadata may reside in Redwood regions. Can you list exactly which control-plane artifacts we should expect to flow to Redwood-managed regions (e.g., billing records, tenant name, SLA metrics) and confirm they will never contain raw prompt data or model outputs?

> 2) Deletion attestations — is the signed attestation acceptable to our auditors if it includes file-level manifests and timestamps? We need a time-bound statement (for example: "All customer data stored in region X has been irreversibly deleted as of yyyy-mm-dd, artifacts attached").

> 3) DR activation — in the event of an automated failover test initiated by Ferry, can you confirm the button will create replicas in the DR region only during the test and then automatically purge them afterwards unless we explicitly opt into persistent DR replication?

If you can answer these three items in writing, legal will be comfortable adding the addendum to the SOW and moving to signature.

— Maria

Maria — thanks for the follow-ups. Answers below and next steps.

1) Control-plane artifacts
- We will enumerate and bind the control-plane fields in the SOW. Typical control-plane artifacts we collect and may store in Redwood control plane regions for management are: tenant identifier (opaque id), billing usage aggregates (no raw prompt text), SLA metrics (latency percentiles, error rates), and support case metadata (case id, timestamps).
- We confirm: raw prompt payloads and model outputs are never sent to Redwood's managed control plane for Private deployments unless explicitly configured as a "managed logging" option in the SOW (we will mark that as an opt-in checkbox).

2) Deletion attestations
- Yes — the signed attestation we provide will include a time-bound statement and attached manifests (file-level list, deletion timestamps, job IDs). Example language we propose: "Redwood Inference certifies that all customer data stored on Redwood-managed compute and storage for tenant <FERRY-xxxx> in region US-WEST-2 was irreversibly deleted on 2027-09-20T15:03:00Z. Evidence artifacts: [manifest-20270920.csv, wipe-job-98765.log]."
- We'll include the CSV manifest and the job logs as supporting artifacts.

3) DR activation behavior
- For DR tests invoked by the customer we will create temporary replicas in the DR region for the duration of the test and automatically purge those replicas at the end of the test unless the customer opts into persistent replication. We'll provide a test run-id and the purge-job artifacts.

SOW & signature
- I've incorporated the above language into the SOW addendum and attached the draft (Ferry_SOW_Draft_v2.pdf). If this aligns, I'll push the envelope to DocuSign and route to Legal Ops for signature.

Propose: signature timeline = 5 business days after SOW delivery; deletion SLA baseline = certificate within 10 business days of decommission.

If you want, Marissa and Karthik are looped for any technical exceptions or special handling (e.g., customer HSM specifics).

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if Legal wants to review wording live.

Best,
